adjudications.finding: Rails migration files can contain framework bookkeeping writes that look broad in isolation.
adjudications.note: A maintainer should suppress or downgrade framework-managed schema/version bookkeeping when the operation is not application data repair risk.

adjudications.finding: Business-semantic backfills may be unsafe even when the SQL/API shape is bounded.
adjudications.note: Without production invariants, a bounded update can still violate product semantics; this is tracked as a false-negative class for reviewer sampling.

adjudications.finding: Some migration-like SQL files are fixtures or compatibility examples rather than live production migrations.
adjudications.note: The matrix keeps these visible but records that deployment context is needed before treating every matched SQL file as an actionable risk.

adjudications.finding: Dialect-specific runtime behavior can be missed when static SQL text is valid but deployment engine/version context is absent.
adjudications.note: This tracks a known blind spot for public migration slices without engine runtime metadata.

adjudications.finding: Rails helper calls can be intentionally safe even when Patchline assigns risk from the surrounding migration pattern.
adjudications.note: Reviewer adjudication should separate framework-safe helper behavior from genuinely broad application writes.

adjudications.finding: A migration can be safe alone but unsafe when coupled with application background jobs or deployment order.
adjudications.note: Public migration-only slices cannot fully observe runtime job/deploy coupling, so this remains a sampled false-negative class.

adjudications.finding: Small-repo maintenance migrations can be flagged as broad because static analysis lacks operator intent and dataset scale.
adjudications.note: The finding is still useful for review, but sampled adjudication records that small controlled maintenance changes may be non-actionable.

adjudications.finding: Application invariants outside the migration folder can make apparently safe schema/data changes risky.
adjudications.note: This is tracked as a false-negative class when the evaluated slice omits application-level invariants.
